Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2604.05172v2. State-based productivity/safety scoring and same-task scaffold refinement limits establish substantive benchmark protocol research. Paper work differs from the ClawsBench family and provides no new family completion. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Scaffolding was iteratively refined on the evaluated task set, so the authors treat its measured lift as an upper bound on unseen-task transfer. The mocks omit rate limits, latency and concurrent access; the 44-task study lacks a human baseline and has only five of eleven harness/model pairs with full 2 × 2 coverage.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2604.05172.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • The benchmark has 20 non-safety and 24 safety tasks. TSR is non-safety score >=0.8; UAR is safety score <0; SCR is safety score >=0.8.
  • Five of eleven harness/model combinations have complete 2x2 factor coverage. Mock services omit rate limiting, latency and concurrency; there is no human baseline.
  • Scaffolding was refined on the evaluated tasks, so measured lift is not held-out transfer evidence. Safety tasks target violations, and low UAR can partly reflect over-refusal.
  • Programmatic database-state evaluators score final outcomes, and agents call the mock REST APIs through terminal commands rather than a browser/GUI.
  • Figure 3 labels Flash-Lite UAR as 22%, while Table 4 and adjacent prose report 23%; this internal discrepancy is preserved.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ClawsBench uses 44 structured tasks across five stateful SQLite-backed mock services and deterministic before/after state evaluation. Task Success Rate is measured on nonsafety tasks at score≥0.8, while Unsafe Action Rate is measured separately on safety tasks at score<0; domain skills and a meta prompt are varied with an intentionally incomplete factorial design.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

In the six-model OpenClaw comparison, the paper reports that full skills-plus-meta scaffolding raises Task Success Rate from 0–8% without scaffolding to 39–63%. These are task/condition-level reported results with cluster-bootstrap uncertainty, not current-product safety rankings or proof of transfer to unseen tasks.
